title: Securities Trading Policy
date_next_review: As and when required (the Board will review this Policy as and when required)

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Employees, contractors, directors of the Company, Executive Management and any other person that agrees to be bound by this Policy from time to time, and Controlled Entities of such persons. Subject to the insider trading prohibition, the Restricted Period bans, the prohibition on trading for short term or speculative gain, the Written Clearance gate on hedging, derivatives and arrangements limiting economic risk, and the Written Clearance gate on granting security over Megaport Securities.

tiers.name: Executive Management
tiers.description: The CEO, chief financial officer, chief operations officer, chief legal officer, any other Key Management Personnel and other direct reports of the CEO. Must obtain prior Written Clearance to trade at any time, not only during Restricted Periods, and is subject to the longer Board-level Closed Periods.

tiers.name: directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company. Must obtain prior Written Clearance to trade at any time, are subject to the longer Board-level Closed Periods, and must notify the Company Secretary of any trade within 2 days so an Appendix 3Y can be lodged.

tiers.name: The Chair
tiers.description: The chair of the Board, distinguished only for who approves: routine authorisation comes from the Chair of the Audit Committee, and Written Clearance under Authorised Trading from two non-executive directors or a non-executive director and the CEO or CFO.

tiers.name: all other Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Restricted Persons who are not Board members or Executive Management, principally employees and contractors. Subject to the shorter four-week and two-week Closed Periods, need Written Clearance only to trade in a Restricted Period or to engage in speculative trading or grant security, and must notify completed transactions within 14 days.

tiers.name: Relative
tiers.description: All relatives of the person including such person's spouse, de facto spouse, children and step-children. Relatives of Restricted Persons must not trade during a Restricted Period without Written Clearance, and Relatives of directors and Executive Management need prior Written Clearance to trade at any time.

tiers.name: Controlled Entities
tiers.description: A company or trust controlled by a Restricted Person. Controlled Entities are themselves within the definition of Restricted Persons, and a Restricted Person prohibited from trading must not trade through a trust or company over which they have influence or control.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may declare 'any other period during which the Board decides some or all Restricted Persons are prohibited from trading in Megaport Securities', which forms part of the definition of Restricted Period. The policy is silent on whether such a period, or the reason for it, is confidential, and silent on any notification to affected persons.

rules.section: Speculative Trading; Which securities does this Policy apply to?
rules.detail: Dealing in derivatives is expressly named as an activity a Restricted Person must not engage in without Written Clearance, and put and call options are given as examples. Megaport Securities expressly include hedging or derivative instruments in relation to Megaport securities, with no venue limitation, so OTC options with a bank are squarely caught. Written Clearance is available only on the exceptional circumstances test in 'When can Written Clearance be given?'.
rules.evidence: In particular you must not engage in the following activities without Written Clearance: engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which limit the economic risk related to Megaport Securities (including, for example, the use of put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of Megaport Securities)

rules.section: Speculative Trading; Authorised Trading; When can Written Clearance be given?
rules.detail: Hedging arrangements and other arrangements limiting economic risk related to Megaport Securities require Written Clearance. The policy draws no distinction between vested, unvested or holding-locked securities for hedging, and no distinction between plan and non-plan securities. The gate is high: a Restricted Person who wishes to engage in speculative trading 'may apply for permission to trade if exceptional circumstances exist', and Written Clearance can only be given if the trade is not for speculative gain, not likely to be seen as unfair, and exceptional circumstances justify it.
rules.evidence: If you are a Restricted Person or their Relative and wish to trade in Megaport Securities during a Restricted Period or if you are a Restricted Person who wishes to engage in speculative trading or grant security over your Megaport Securities, but cannot do so because of this Policy, you may apply for permission to trade if exceptional circumstances exist. This is called Written Clearance.

rules.detail: Monetisation and prepaid forwards are not named. Any such structure is an 'other arrangement which limits the economic risk related to Megaport Securities' and so falls in the Written Clearance gate; if it is funded by security over the shares the Security Arrangements paragraph applies as well.
rules.evidence: enter into other arrangements which limit the economic risk related to Megaport Securities

rules.detail: Short selling as such is not named, but entering into any arrangement designed to profit from a decrease in the share price is expressly listed as requiring Written Clearance. In practice clearance is unavailable, because it can only be given where the proposed trade is not for speculative gain and exceptional circumstances exist, so a short position is effectively barred.
rules.evidence: enter into any arrangement designed to profit from a decrease in the share price of Megaport Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending and borrowing are not mentioned. The policy has no definition of 'trade', and the Security Arrangements paragraph is directed at granting security to secure the person's own obligations rather than at lending out securities.

Contracts for difference are named expressly as an example of an arrangement limiting economic risk that requires Written Clearance, subject to the same exceptional circumstances and no-speculative-gain conditions.
rules.evidence: including, for example, the use of put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of Megaport Securities

rules.detail: Margin lenders are named expressly. Granting security over Megaport Securities to a margin lender requires Written Clearance but is not banned. A disposal of Megaport Securities by a secured lender under a loan agreement secured by the Megaport Securities is outside the Policy altogether.
rules.evidence: you must not, unless you have Written Clearance, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (such as a charge, mortgage or pledge) over any of your Megaport Securities (including those Megaport Securities which are unvested or the subject of a holding lock) to secure your obligations to any third party, including a margin lender.

rules.detail: Granting any form of security, directly or indirectly, over vested unrestricted Megaport Securities to secure obligations to any third party requires Written Clearance. There is no outright ban and no limit on the identity of the secured party.
rules.evidence: you must not, unless you have Written Clearance, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (such as a charge, mortgage or pledge) over any of your Megaport Securities

rules.detail: Unvested Megaport Securities are expressly brought within the Security Arrangements clearance gate rather than being excluded from collateral. The policy therefore does not prohibit pledging unvested securities, though the terms of the relevant employee incentive scheme would need to permit it and Written Clearance requires exceptional circumstances.
rules.evidence: (including those Megaport Securities which are unvested or the subject of a holding lock)

rules.detail: Securities the subject of a holding lock are expressly within the Security Arrangements clearance gate. The policy does not say a holding lock will be released to permit enforcement, so the practical effect is that a secured party may hold a charge over shares it cannot have transferred while the lock subsists.
rules.evidence: (including those Megaport Securities which are unvested or the subject of a holding lock) to secure your obligations to any third party, including a margin lender.

rules.detail: The Security Arrangements paragraph is a clearance gate, not a prohibition, and reaches any form of security granted directly or indirectly to secure obligations to any third party, so a bank loan secured on collared shares is caught. Written Clearance for a security arrangement is expressly routed through the Authorised Trading paragraph, which requires exceptional circumstances.
rules.evidence: If you are a Restricted Person ... who wishes to engage in speculative trading or grant security over your Megaport Securities, but cannot do so because of this Policy, you may apply for permission to trade if exceptional circumstances exist.

rules.detail: Flat prohibition on trading in Megaport Securities for short term or speculative gain, with no defined holding period, no matching basis and no carve-outs. It is drafted as an absolute statement, with the following bullets identifying specific activities that additionally require Written Clearance, and it feeds the condition that Written Clearance can only be given where the trade is not for speculative gain.
rules.evidence: If you are a Restricted Person, you must not trade in Megaport Securities for short term or speculative gain.

clearance.approver: The Chair (routine authorisation to trade); two directors where the person is the CEO or a director other than the Chair seeking Written Clearance under Authorised Trading
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (copies of the Written Clearance must be forwarded before the transaction; details of the trade after it, for the Appendix 3Y)
clearance.section: Authorisation requirement; Authorised Trading; Notification of trades
clearance.evidence: Executive Management, directors and their Relatives wishing to trade in Megaport Securities at any time must obtain prior Written Clearance ... If you are a director and trade in Megaport Securities, you must notify the Company Secretary within 2 days of the trade so that an Appendix 3Y or other prescribed form notifying ASX of the trade can be lodged.

clearance.approver: Chair of the Audit Committee (routine authorisation); two non-executive directors or a non-executive director and the CEO or CFO (Written Clearance under Authorised Trading)
clearance.evidence: The Chair | Two non-executive directors or a non-executive director and the CEO or CFO

clearance.approver: CEO (routine authorisation for all other Executive Management; The Chair for the CEO); two directors where the CEO seeks Written Clearance under Authorised Trading
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (copies of Written Clearance before the transaction; details of completed transactions after it)
clearance.evidence: All other Executive Management | CEO ... Copies of Written Clearance must be forwarded to the Company Secretary prior to the authorised purchase or sale transaction.

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (details of all completed transactions, whether or not clearance was required)
clearance.evidence: Any other Restricted Person | CEO ... If you trade in Megaport Securities you must notify the Company Secretary of the details of all completed transactions within 14 days after each transaction. This is necessary whether or not authorisation or Written Clearance was required prior to trading.

clearance.approver: The relevant Authorised Officer for the Restricted Person to whom they are related
clearance.evidence: If you are a Restricted Person or a Relative of a Restricted Person, you must not trade during a Restricted Period unless you have Written Clearance ... Executive Management, directors and their Relatives wishing to trade in Megaport Securities at any time must obtain prior Written Clearance

short_term.basis: purpose test: trading for short term or speculative gain
short_term.evidence: If you are a Restricted Person, you must not trade in Megaport Securities for short term or speculative gain.

exceptions.evidence: disposal of Megaport Securities by a secured lender under a loan agreement secured by the Megaport Securities. See also the paragraph entitled "Security Arrangements".
exceptional circumstances may exist where the proposed trade is: to realise cash in a time of exceptional financial hardship;
to comply with the requirement of a court order or enforceable undertaking;
sought because delaying the trade would be exceptionally detrimental to the person's family affairs.
transfers in Megaport Securities where the beneficial ownership does not change;

a transfer of Megaport Securities already held by you into a superannuation fund or similar saving scheme in which you are a beneficiary; transfers of Megaport Securities by you to your Relative with Written Clearance;
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer or scheme of arrangement;

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the existing security holders in a company, such as a pro-rata rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend, an equal access buy back or distribution reinvestment plan (where you have not commenced or amended your participation in the security purchase plan or distribution reinvestment plan during a Restricted Period);

the acquisition, election to acquire or exercise (but not the sale of securities following exercise) of a Megaport Security or an option, unit or a right (including restricted stock units) in respect of Megaport Securities under an employee incentive scheme, or the conversion of a convertible security, where the exercise of the option, unit or right, or the conversion of the security into a Megaport Security, falls during a Restricted Period;
investing or trading in a fund, scheme or an exchange traded fund (ETF) which holds Megaport Securities where the assets of that fund or scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party;
where Megaport has an employee incentive scheme with you as a trustee of that scheme, an acquisition of Megaport Securities by you in your capacity as trustee;

financing_disclosure: Restricted Persons (all tiers, including directors, Executive Management, employees, contractors and Controlled Entities); trigger: inception, before directly or indirectly granting any form of security over Megaport Securities to any third party including a margin lender; to: the applicable Authorised Officer by way of Written Clearance; deadline: before the security is granted.

Restricted Persons; trigger: grant of Written Clearance; to: the Company Secretary, who must receive a copy of the Written Clearance prior to the authorised purchase or sale transaction and maintains a register of securities transactions.
directors; trigger: any trade in Megaport Securities; to: the Company Secretary, for lodgement of an Appendix 3Y; deadline: within 2 days of the trade.
Restricted Persons other than directors; trigger: any completed transaction, whether or not clearance was required; to: the Company Secretary; deadline: within 14 days after each transaction.

exemption_authority: Authorised Officers have absolute discretion to give, refuse or withdraw Written Clearance, and their decisions are final. Written Clearance for trading in a Restricted Period, for speculative trading (including hedging and derivatives) and for granting security is available only where exceptional circumstances exist, being at the Authorised Officer's discretion but illustrated by exceptional financial hardship, a court order or enforceable undertaking, or exceptional detriment to family affairs, and only where the trade is not contrary to law, not for speculative gain, not to take advantage of Inside information and not likely to be seen by the public, press, other shareholders or ASX as unfair.

bespoke_clauses.topic: exceptional circumstances gate on hedging and security
bespoke_clauses.clause: If you are a Restricted Person ... who wishes to engage in speculative trading or grant security over your Megaport Securities, but cannot do so because of this Policy, you may apply for permission to trade if exceptional circumstances exist. ... Written Clearance can only be given if ... the proposed trade is not for speculative gain ... and exceptional circumstances exist justifying the issue of the Written Clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the decisive clause for a funded collar: both the derivative legs and the security over the shares are routed to a clearance that on its face is only available in exceptional circumstances such as financial hardship or a court order, so an ordinary portfolio-diversification collar is very unlikely to be approvable.

bespoke_clauses.topic: security arrangements are gated, not banned
bespoke_clauses.clause: you must not, unless you have Written Clearance, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (such as a charge, mortgage or pledge) over any of your Megaport Securities (including those Megaport Securities which are unvested or the subject of a holding lock) to secure your obligations to any third party, including a margin lender.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg is not prohibited outright and can even in principle cover unvested or holding-locked shares, but it needs Written Clearance and reaches indirect security, so a security trustee or back-to-back arrangement does not avoid it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy does not apply to: ... disposal of Megaport Securities by a secured lender under a loan agreement secured by the Megaport Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale is entirely outside the Policy, so lender enforcement during a Closed Period or Board-imposed Restricted Period does not breach it, although the Corporations Act insider trading prohibition still applies to the disposal.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Authorisation requirement table (Chair to Chair of the Audit Committee; CEO or a director other than the Chairperson to the Chair; all other Executive Management to the CEO) differs from the Authorised Trading table (Chair to two non-executive directors or a non-executive director and the CEO or CFO; CEO or a director other than the Chair to two directors; any other Restricted Person to the CEO).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A hedging or security arrangement is an Authorised Trading matter, so a director needs sign-off from two directors rather than the Chair alone, which raises the approval bar and lengthens the timetable for documenting a collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Unless otherwise specified in the Written Clearance and provided the Written Clearance has not been withdrawn, trades and other dealings in Megaport Securities that have received Written Clearance must be made within 7 days of the date of that Written Clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar legs and the security must be executed within 7 days of clearance unless a longer period is written into the clearance, so documentation should be fully negotiated before clearance is sought.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Authorised Officers have absolute discretion to give or refuse Written Clearance and to withdraw Written Clearance if new information comes to light. The Authorised Officer's decisions are final and if you are refused Written Clearance you must keep that refusal confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance can be pulled before execution and a refusal cannot be explained to the bank, so the bank should not commit funding or hedge until the trade is done.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the proposed trade is not for speculative gain, to take advantage of Inside information or likely to be seen by the public, press, other shareholders or ASX as unfair.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An optics test sits alongside the legal tests, and a director monetising a large stake through a bank collar is exactly the kind of transaction that could be judged likely to be seen as unfair.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person who would be prohibited from trading under this Policy must not trade through any member of their family, or through a trust or company over which they have influence or control.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Controlled Entities are themselves Restricted Persons, so holding the collared shares through a family trust or company gains nothing and the same Written Clearance is needed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All requests to buy or sell Megaport Securities must include: ... the intended volume of securities to be purchased or sold; an estimated time frame for the sale or purchase; and a statement that the person is not in possession of any Inside information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Authorised Officer must be given the size and timing of the trade, so the notional, tenor and settlement mechanics of the collar cannot be kept confidential from the Company.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Closed Period ... (a) in respect of Board members and Executive Management ... from 9 June ... from 10 December ... four weeks prior to the conclusion of the annual general meeting; (b) in respect of all other Restricted Persons ... four weeks prior to the announcement ... two weeks prior to the conclusion of the annual general meeting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Directors and Executive Management face materially longer closed periods, roughly 9 June to the full year result and 10 December to the half year result plus an AGM window, so open windows for entering or unwinding a collar are narrow.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If you trade in Megaport Securities you must notify the Company Secretary of the details of all completed transactions within 14 days after each transaction. This is necessary whether or not authorisation or Written Clearance was required prior to trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every leg, roll and settlement of the collar must be reported to the Company Secretary and recorded on the register, and directors must report within 2 days for Appendix 3Y purposes.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy applies to the securities of other companies if: the other company is a joint venture or collaborative partner of Megaport; ... or Megaport has a substantial interest (5% or more) in the other company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The clearance and closed period regime extends to securities of certain counterparties, so a basket hedge that includes those names would also be caught.

summary: A funded collar is theoretically permitted but practically very hard under this policy, because both legs of the structure are routed to the same narrow gate. Dealing in derivatives, hedging arrangements and other arrangements limiting economic risk related to Megaport Securities, including put and call options and CFDs by name, require Written Clearance, and granting any form of security directly or indirectly over Megaport Securities to any third party including a margin lender also requires Written Clearance; neither is banned outright, and unvested and holding-locked securities are expressly within the security gate rather than excluded. The difficulty is that the Authorised Trading paragraph makes Written Clearance for speculative trading and for security arrangements available only where exceptional circumstances exist, illustrated by exceptional financial hardship, a court order or exceptional detriment to family affairs, and only where the trade is not for speculative gain and not likely to be seen by the public, press, other shareholders or ASX as unfair. A director would need sign-off from two directors (two non-executive directors or a non-executive director and the CEO or CFO for the Chair), must disclose volume and timing, must execute within 7 days of clearance, faces long Closed Periods running from 9 June and 10 December plus an AGM window and any Board-imposed Restricted Period, and must notify the Company Secretary within 2 days of each trade. The one clearly favourable feature for a bank is that a disposal of Megaport Securities by a secured lender under a loan agreement secured by those securities falls entirely outside the Policy, so enforcement is not a policy breach.
